Q: glibc startup code appears to overwrite stack variable when debugging with GDB + ASAN A:

As confirmed in the comments, the false triggering of the watchpoint happened after the program was restarted. It is normal for stack memory to be used for other purposes before your main() runs.

There are two ways to avoid the false watchpoint trigger:

  1. Set a breakpoint on main() and set watchpoint when it gets hit. Then continue running. If you want to be able to easily restart the program, you can use the gdb commands feature to enable the watchpoint on the breakpoint hit.
  2. Make your context variable static struct file_ctx ctx; for testing. Then it is allocated persistent storage, which is not used by other code. Note that if you are using multiple threads or calling the function recursively, the storage will be shared between calls.

Q: C++ string too big, trailing characters truncated A:

The Standard does not specify a maximum limit of string literals but does suggest a minimum size. From Annex B - Implementation quantities

The limits may constrain quantities that include those described below or others. The bracketed number following each quantity is recommended as the minimum for that quantity. However, these quantities are only guidelines and do not determine compliance.

  • Characters in a string literal (after concatenation) [65 536].

However the same section in the standard also states the following

Because computers are finite, C++ implementations are inevitably limited in the size of the programs they can successfully process. Every implementation shall document those limitations where known. This documentation may cite fixed limits where they exist, say how to compute variable limits as a function of available resources, or say that fixed limits do not exist or are unknown.

It's safe to assume that a 5MB string literal is going to exceed maximum limits imposed by the compiler. You should refer to the documentation of your tool chain to determine what limits are imposed for string literals.

If you are using the Visual C++ compiler the maximum size of a string literal is 16,384 bytes. From the MSDN documentation

  • Visual Studio prior to 2022 version 17.0: the maximum length of a string literal after concatenation is 65,535 bytes. This applies to both narrow and wide string literals.
  • From Visual Studio 2022 version 17.0 onwards: the maximum length of a string literal after concatenation is only limited by available memory. However, the size limit before concatenation is still 16,384 bytes

"After concatenation" is referring to concatenating strings "like" "this".

Q: Apex trigger works for single records but hits governor limits during bulk insert/update A:

SOQL within for loop causing Too many SOQL exception

DML inside for loop causing Too many DML exception

Solution: Bulkify the code using Maps:

  1. first create a set of contact Ids

  2. Retrieve the AccountIds for each contactId

  3. Then set AccountId from map in the contacts iteration in for loop

Q: How can I copy files from a host to a Docker container? A:

The cleanest way is to mount a host directory on the container when starting the container:

On the host:

docker run -v /path/to/hostdir:/mnt --name my_container my_image
docker exec -it my_container bash

Inside the container:

cp /mnt/sourcefile /path/to/destfile

Q: Mosquitto MQTT SSL with Certificates throwing Errors A:

It seems that by default letsencrypt makes the directories live & archive read only to the root user. When mosquitto starts up it changes from the root user to the mosquitto user and this wont have the permissions to read these files.

You can run mosquitto as root by adding the config directive. not the best security policy:

user root

You can change the permissions on the letsencrypt directories:

chmod 0644 /etc/letsencrypt/live
chmod 0644 /etc/letsencrypt/live/<domain name>
chmod 0644 /etc/letsencrypt/archive
chmod 0644 /etc/letsencrypt/archive/<domain name>

This makes the certificate files world readable, again, not the best security policy, but works.

Something fancier would be to copy the certs into the directory /etc/mosquitto/certs and then make them read only to the mosquitto user. You will need to set a trigger when the certificates are updated to copy them when they change. But you will need to set a reload trigger for the other solutions as well as these will need to be restarted.

certbot --post-hook POST_HOOK

Q: HAVING MAX(Value) is not working in SQL Server query A:

The most straightforward way is using a subquery:

SELECT 
    eum.[OrganisationID] 
    ,eum.[MailboxLocationName] AS Location 
    ,eum.MailboxCode as LocationCode 
    ,eum.DayofMon 
    ,COUNT(DISTINCT [eum.UPN]) AS [Count]
FROM 
    [ExchangeUserMailbox] AS eum
WHERE eum.DayofMon =
      (SELECT MAX(eum2.DayofMon)
       FROM   [ExchangeUserMailbox] AS eum2
       WHERE  eum2.[OrganisationID] = eum.[OrganisationID]
       AND    eum2.[MailboxLocationName] = eum.[MailboxLocationName]
       AND    eum2.MailboxCode = eum.MailboxCode
      )
GROUP BY 
    eum.[OrganisationID], eum.[MailboxLocationName], eum.DayofMon, eum.MailboxCode

The "hard coded" solutions work, but are more brittle. This way, you are sure to always get the records with the highest DayofMon value (even if it is an unexpected value) and you get the actual value of DayofMon instead of a hard coded value.

Q: python 3.14 shared mutex lock A:

Here is a possible implementation based on this question.

test demonstrates that 4 reader threads can have shared access while a writer thread wanting exclusive use must wait for the reader threads to release the "shared lock". Then when the writer thread acquires exclusive use of the resource, the 4 reader threads must wait until the writer thread releases the resource. Another test is performed where we have a single reader and two writers.

from contextlib import contextmanager
from threading import Condition, Thread
import time

class SharedLock:
    def __init__(self):
        self._cond = Condition()
        self._readers = 0
        self._writers = 0
        self._writers_waiting = 0

    @contextmanager
    def __call__(self, lock_type: str):
        if lock_type == 'shared':
            with self._cond:
                # We have to give a writer a chance to handle
                # the situation where there the number of readers never
                # goes back to 0 beacause a new reader acquires the shared lock
                # before all previous readers have released the lock:
                while self._writers or self._writers_waiting:
                    self._cond.wait()
                self._readers += 1
            yield self
            with self._cond:
                self._readers -= 1
                if not self._readers:
                    self._cond.notify()
        elif lock_type == 'exclusive':
            with self._cond:
                # Assume we cannot acquire an exclusive lock
                # because there are readers or another writer holding the lock
                self._writers_waiting += 1
                while self._readers or self._writers:
                    self._cond.wait()
                self._writers_waiting -= 1
                self._writers = 1  # There can never be more than 1
                yield self
                self._writers = 0
                self._cond.notify_all()  # Wake up readers and writers
        else:
            raise ValueError(f'Invalid lock_type {lock_type!r}')

if __name__ == '__main__':
    shared_lock = SharedLock()

    def reader():
        with shared_lock('shared'):
            print('start reading', time.time())
            time.sleep(1)
            print('end reading', time.time())

    def writer():
        # Give reader threads a chance to acquire shared use:
        time.sleep(.1)

        with shared_lock('exclusive'):
            print('start writing', time.time())
            time.sleep(1)
            print('end writing', time.time())

if __name__ == '__main__':
    shared_lock = SharedLock()

    def reader():
        with shared_lock('shared'):
            print('start reading', time.time())
            time.sleep(1)
            print('end reading', time.time())

        # Give writer thread a chance to acquire exclusive use:
        time.sleep(.1)

        with shared_lock('shared'):
            print('start reading', time.time())
            time.sleep(1)
            print('end reading', time.time())

    def writer():
        # Give reader threads a chance to acquire shared use:
        time.sleep(.1)

        with shared_lock('exclusive'):
            print('start writing', time.time())
            time.sleep(1)
            print('end writing', time.time())

    def test():
        reader_threads = [
            Thread(target=reader) for _ in range(4)
        ]

        writer_threads = [
            Thread(target=writer) for _ in range(2)
        ]

        for t in reader_threads:
            t.start()
        for t in writer_threads:
            t.start()

        for t in reader_threads:
            t.join()
        for t in writer_threads:
            t.join()

    test()
